text:
sam: Heads up — streaming generation with hf/chat-mix-v2 stops early when stop=[''] is used. Repro steps below.

sam: Repro payload (curl):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "hf/chat-mix-v2",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Explain packer compression"}
  ],
  "stop": [""],
  "stream": true
}
```

sam: Short log snippet from the runtime (streaming output):
```
[stream] token_text: "Hello"
[stream] token_text: " world"
[stream] token_text: ""   <-- emitted, runtime treats as stop and closes stream
[stream] token_text: ""   <-- second eos emitted but never reached by client
```

suzanne: Can you paste tokenizer/config snippets? suspect duplicate eos or chat template adding another sentinel.

sam: Tokenizer excerpt from huggingface conversion:
```
{
  "eos_token": "",
  "additional_special_tokens": ["", "<|assistant|>"]
}
```
Chat template suffix used in conversion: "\n\n<|endoftext|><|endoftext|>\nAssistant:"
Tokenized tail: [..., 50256, 50256]

jon: This matches what I saw before — our streaming stop detector currently matches on detokenized text (""), then quits on the first match. When there are consecutive eos ids the first gets emitted and stream closes prematurely. Two possible fixes: 1) dedupe repeated eos in conversion, or 2) switch to token-id-based stop detection for streaming.

luis: Also note: quantized backend (q4_0) uses the fast tokenizer binary which sometimes emits different splits for trailing newlines. Might make text-based detection brittle across runtimes.

suzanne: Proposed conversion fix:
- normalize tokenizer.extra to remove duplicate eos from additional_special_tokens
- ensure chat templates don't append multiple eos sentinels
- convert stop sequences to token-id lists when possible
Example transform (pseudo):
```
if tokenizer.additional_special_tokens contains eos_token:
  remove duplicates
stop_token_ids = tokenizer.encode(eos_token)
```

sam: I'll land a small PR to normalize the tokens + add a streaming test that asserts we don't close after the first of two eos tokens when the stop sequence is something else. I'll also experiment with token-id-based detection. @jon want to pair on the test? :+1:

jon: Yup, I'll help. Also add a regression test for streaming+q4_0 backend.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: canary/stream-eos-normalize on 2026-03-20T04:00:00Z

suzanne: Thanks — assigning sam+jon to the ticket and adding a failing example to evals/streaming/fixtures.
